name: BedrockClaude
title: Bedrock Chat
description: Ask Claude on AWS Bedrock, optionally about an image or document
whenToUse: Reach for this when a step needs Claude to answer in ONE pass and the call must run in YOUR AWS account and region: summarise, analyse, classify, answer, including about an image or a document fetched alongside the prompt. It can be given a tool schema to return structured arguments instead of prose. Working through a problem across several tool calls is an agent's job, not this one's, and a step that needs a GPT model rather than Claude is not this node's job either.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the prompt templates

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: { text, toolUse, usage }. `toolUse` is present only when the model chose a tool, and carries its name and arguments. The tool's arguments are also hoisted to the top of the output, so a schema field like `faqs` reads as `output.faqs` directly.

model.title: Model
model.description: Select the Claude model to use

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: The request to answer. Usually wired in from an upstream node.

systemPrompt.title: System Prompt
systemPrompt.description: Standing instructions for every run: the model's role, tone and limits. Optional. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.

includeImageUrl.title: Include an Image
includeImageUrl.description: Fetch an image and let the model see it alongside the prompt

includeDocumentUrl.title: Include a Document
includeDocumentUrl.description: Fetch a document and let the model read it alongside the prompt

documentName.title: Document Name
documentName.description: What the model should call the document when referring to it

enableTools.title: Enable Tools
enableTools.description: Offer the model a tool schema, so it can return structured arguments

toolSchema.title: Tool Schema
toolSchema.description: The tools to offer, as JSON Anthropic tool entries (name, description, input_schema)

toolChoice.title: Tool Choice
toolChoice.description: Let the model decide, or force it to use one

authRequired.description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.

package.name: aws-bedrock
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# BEDROCK AS MANIFESTS, and the cheapest AWS package to convert: both API calls it makes
# (Converse and InvokeModel) are plain signed JSON POSTs. Everything it needed already
# existed by the time it was reached — the signer from DynamoDB, and `transport: binary`
# for the attachments Claude can read.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-bedrock/`.

name: aws-bedrock
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: Claude and GPT models plus Titan embeddings on AWS Bedrock
version: 2.1.0
category: ai
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749137717/gravity/icons/vdyfnijyuyk8ajqtp3nu.webp

features:
  - Claude on Bedrock via the native Messages API, with images, documents and tools
  - GPT on Bedrock, one prompt to one completion
  - Titan text embeddings, inline or over a service edge
  - Apply Bedrock guardrails to any text — screen, block or mask by your org's policy

# Two labels deep at least: bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"
  # The bedrock-mantle endpoint, AWS's host for the native Anthropic Messages API:
  # bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws.
  - "**.api.aws"
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED attachment fetches only. BedrockClaude reads an image
  # or document from a url a person supplies, which cannot be declared in advance. Those
  # calls send no credential, and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does.
  - "*"

requires:
  # SigV4 for the embeddings nodes; the LLM nodes authenticate with a Bedrock API key,
  # x-api-key on the Mantle endpoint and bearer on bedrock-runtime.
  credential: [awsSigV4, apiKeyHeader, bearer]
  transport: [json, binary]
  # Bedrock embeds ONE text per request, so a batch is a fan-out.
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.bedrockCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# A Bedrock API key, NOT an IAM access-key pair. Minted on the Bedrock console's API keys
# page, it authenticates as a plain header with no SigV4 signing: `x-api-key` against the
# bedrock-mantle Anthropic endpoint, `Authorization: Bearer` against bedrock-runtime.
#
# The embeddings nodes keep the signed awsCredential; this one belongs to the LLM nodes.

name: bedrockCredential
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: API key credentials for AWS Bedrock model calls
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: A Bedrock API key from the Bedrock console
    placeholder: ABSK...

  - name: region
    displayName: Region
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The AWS region your Bedrock models are enabled in
    placeholder: us-east-1

shared.bedrock.yaml:
# The one call shape every Bedrock node makes.
#
# Bedrock is REST, unlike DynamoDB: the model id is in the PATH and the operation is the
# last segment, so there is no X-Amz-Target header here. `bedrock-runtime` is the signing
# service name and is NOT the same as the console's "bedrock" — signing against the wrong
# one is a 403 that says nothing about which name was wrong.

call: &call
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: bedrock-runtime
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  # Bedrock throttles hard under load and answers 429; retrying is the difference between a
  # workflow that survives a burst and one that fails a step at random.
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

host: &host >-
  return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com'

# The same call, authenticated with a Bedrock API key instead of request signing.
# bedrock-runtime accepts the key as a plain bearer header, so the executor needs no
# signer for the nodes that use this shape.
keyCall: &keyCall
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.bedrockCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical Bedrock model lists, one per model family, organised by TIER.
#
# Same contract as openai/shared/models.yaml: the data lives here, the fallback logic
# (`resolve: modelTier` on the config field) lives in the executor. A new generation is
# a per-tier edit here, and every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# Bedrock ids carry the vendor prefix. Enable each model for your region in the Bedrock
# console before first use; that is an account setting, not something a manifest can do.

claude:
  # Listed large first so the strongest reads first. The picker's options.
  enum:
    - anthropic.claude-opus-5
    - anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    - anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5

  # Version numbers in the labels by request. When a generation ships, the label is
  # edited alongside the id, or the two lie together.
  enumNames:
    - Claude Opus 5 (Frontier, complex work)
    - Claude Sonnet 5 (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - Claude Haiku 4.5 (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  # Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
  default: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

gpt:
  enum:
    - openai.gpt-5.6-sol
    - openai.gpt-5.6-terra
    - openai.gpt-5.6-luna

  enumNames:
    - GPT-5.6 Sol (Frontier, complex work)
    - GPT-5.6 Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - GPT-5.6 Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  default: openai.gpt-5.6-terra

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector.
#
# The Messages API reply puts the answer in response.content, a LIST of blocks: text
# blocks, thinking blocks, and a tool_use block when the model reached for a tool. Text
# blocks concatenate, because a long answer can arrive in several.
#
# THE OUTPUT SHAPE IS THE CONTRACT this node has always had: { text, usage: { inputTokens,
# outputTokens, totalTokens }, stopReason, toolUse? }. Downstream templates reference
# those names, so the vendor's snake_case is mapped here, never passed through.

# The chosen tool's ARGUMENTS are also hoisted to the top of the output, so a downstream
# template reads output.faqs directly rather than output.toolUse.toolInput.faqs. Assigned
# FIRST, so the node's fixed keys (text, usage, stopReason, toolUse) win any name
# collision with a tool argument.
- emit: output
  from: response
  value: >-
    return Object.assign(
    {},
    (((response.content || []).filter(b => b.type === 'tool_use')[0] || {}).input) || {},
    {
      text: (response.content || [])
        .filter(b => b.type === 'text').map(b => b.text).join(''),
      usage: {
        inputTokens: (response.usage || {}).input_tokens || 0,
        outputTokens: (response.usage || {}).output_tokens || 0,
        totalTokens: ((response.usage || {}).input_tokens || 0)
          + ((response.usage || {}).output_tokens || 0)
      },
      stopReason: response.stop_reason || ''
    },
    (response.content || []).filter(b => b.type === 'tool_use').length
      ? { toolUse: (response.content || [])
          .filter(b => b.type === 'tool_use')
          .map(b => ({ toolName: b.name, toolInput: b.input }))[0] }
      : {})
files.api/run.yaml:
# Fetch the attachments, then ask. Up to three calls, and only the last is Bedrock.
#
# THE ATTACHMENT CALLS GO TO AN ARBITRARY HOST, which is the whole reason `transport: binary`
# exists: the bytes have to come back in a form that survives being put into a JSON body.
# They are also why this package's allowedHosts is wider than its own vendor.
#
# The answer call speaks the NATIVE ANTHROPIC MESSAGES API, hosted by AWS at the
# bedrock-mantle endpoint. Same body and response shape as api.anthropic.com; what is
# Bedrock about it is only the host, the `anthropic.` model prefix, and the API key.
# This replaced the Converse call: Converse exists to give every vendor one shape, and a
# Claude-only node has no use for that abstraction.

- name: image
  when: "return config.includeImageUrl === true && !!config.imageUrl"
  method: GET
  url: "{{ config.imageUrl }}"
  # The bytes come back as { base64, contentType, bytes }, ready to be embedded below.
  transport: binary

- name: document
  when: "return config.includeDocumentUrl === true && !!config.documentUrl"
  method: GET
  url: "{{ config.documentUrl }}"
  transport: binary

- name: answer
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return 'https://bedrock-mantle.' + (credentials.bedrockCredential.region || 'us-east-1')
      + '.api.aws/anthropic/v1/messages'

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: x-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.bedrockCredential.apiKey }}"

  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    anthropic-version: "2023-06-01"

  transport: json

  # Bounded, because an unbounded call that never answers hangs the whole step with no
  # error anywhere. TEN MINUTES, not the 120s this started with: that bound predated
  # document attachments, and an Opus reading a whole PDF and writing a structured
  # extraction is minutes of legitimate silence on a non-streaming call — seen live
  # 2026-08-05, a 13MB document timing out at 120s while the model was still working.
  timeoutMs: 600000

  # Bedrock throttles hard under load and answers 429; retrying is the difference between a
  # workflow that survives a burst and one that fails a step at random.
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  # The message content is a LIST whose members depend on what was attached, which is
  # exactly the case an object body cannot express. Attachments go before the text, so
  # the prompt can refer to them.
  #
  # No temperature: the current Claude generation rejects sampling parameters, so there
  # is nothing to configure.
  body: >-
    return Object.assign({
      model: config.model,
      max_tokens: config.maxTokens,
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: []
          .concat(calls.image ? [{ type: 'image', source: {
            type: 'base64',
            media_type: String(calls.image.contentType).split(';')[0],
            data: calls.image.base64
          } }] : [])
          .concat(calls.document ? [{ type: 'document', source: {
            type: 'base64',
            media_type: String(calls.document.contentType).split(';')[0],
            data: calls.document.base64
          }, title: config.documentName || 'document' }] : [])
          .concat([{ type: 'text', text: config.prompt }])
      }]
    },
    config.systemPrompt ? { system: config.systemPrompt } : {},
    (config.enableTools === true && (config.toolSchema || []).length)
      ? {
          tools: (Array.isArray(config.toolSchema) ? config.toolSchema : [config.toolSchema])
            .map(t => t.toolSpec
              ? { name: t.toolSpec.name, description: t.toolSpec.description,
                  input_schema: (t.toolSpec.inputSchema || {}).json || t.toolSpec.inputSchema }
              : t),
          tool_choice: config.toolChoice === 'any' ? { type: 'any' } : { type: 'auto' }
        }
      : {})

  # A 200 carrying an error envelope must not read as success.
  error:
    when: "return response.type === 'error'"
    message: "return response.error && response.error.message"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model, prompt]
  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Select the Claude model to use
      enum: { $ref: models#claude/enum }
      enumNames: { $ref: models#claude/enumNames }
      default: { $ref: models#claude/default }
      # A retired id falls back to the current best model in its tier, so replacing a
      # model generation cannot break a saved workflow.
      resolve: modelTier
    # UI copy matches the OpenAI node: short, plain, about the SETTING. The template
    # grammar and its traps are not repeated here; the building model reads them from the
    # template-references skill, which covers every template field on every node.
    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Prompt
      description: The request to answer. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai": { editable: true }
    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: >-
        Standing instructions for every run: the model's role, tone and limits. Optional.
        Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai": { editable: true }
    maxTokens:
      type: number
      title: Max Output Tokens
      default: 4096
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 200000
    includeImageUrl:
      type: boolean
      title: Include an Image
      description: Fetch an image and let the model see it alongside the prompt
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    imageUrl:
      type: string
      title: Image URL
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { includeImageUrl: true }
    includeDocumentUrl:
      type: boolean
      title: Include a Document
      description: Fetch a document and let the model read it alongside the prompt
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    documentUrl:
      type: string
      title: Document URL
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { includeDocumentUrl: true }
    documentName:
      type: string
      title: Document Name
      description: What the model should call the document when referring to it
      default: document
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { includeDocumentUrl: true }
    enableTools:
      type: boolean
      title: Enable Tools
      description: Offer the model a tool schema, so it can return structured arguments
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    # A JSON input, not a code editor: the value IS the tool list, no expression around
    # it. `template` keeps it wirable from an upstream node (config-schema.md, Structured
    # data).
    toolSchema:
      type: object
      title: Tool Schema
      description: The tools to offer, as JSON Anthropic tool entries (name, description, input_schema)
      default: []
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { enableTools: true }
    toolChoice:
      type: string
      title: Tool Choice
      description: Let the model decide, or force it to use one
      enum: [auto, any]
      enumNames: [Auto, Require a tool]
      default: auto
      "ui:dependencies": { enableTools: true }

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, model, prompt, systemPrompt, maxTokens, includeImageUrl, imageUrl, includeDocumentUrl, documentUrl, documentName, enableTools, toolSchema, toolChoice]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the prompt templates
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: >-
      { text, toolUse, usage }. `toolUse` is present only when the model chose a tool, and
      carries its name and arguments. The tool's arguments are also hoisted to the top of
      the output, so a schema field like `faqs` reads as `output.faqs` directly.

credentials:
  - name: bedrockCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS Bedrock
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: BedrockClaude
kind: PromiseNode

name: Bedrock Chat
category: AI
color: "#01A88D"

description: Ask Claude on AWS Bedrock, optionally about an image or document

whenToUse: >-
  Reach for this when a step needs Claude to answer in ONE pass and the call must run in
  YOUR AWS account and region: summarise, analyse, classify, answer, including about an
  image or a document fetched alongside the prompt. It can be given a tool schema to
  return structured arguments instead of prose. Working through a problem across several
  tool calls is an agent's job, not this one's, and a step that needs a GPT model rather
  than Claude is not this node's job either.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: a model call is non-deterministic, so a reused answer is a different
  # answer presented as the same one.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    prompt: Reply with exactly the word READY and nothing else.
    systemPrompt: You follow instructions precisely.
    maxTokens: 64
    includeImageUrl: false
    includeDocumentUrl: false
    enableTools: false
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    output: "return output.output.text.trim().length > 0 && output.output.usage.totalTokens > 0"
